prompt.zh-TW: 上方表格是山嵐茶行的數字：本期淨利 {{money:vars.netIncome}}，年底資產總計 {{money:vars.totalAssets}}、股東權益總額 {{money:vars.totalEquity}}。同業的溪口茶行完全沒有負債，ROE 與 ROA 都是 {{percent:vars.roePeer}}，和山嵐的 ROE 一樣。下列哪一個解讀正確？
prompt.en: The table above shows Mountain Haze Tea: profit for the period {{money:vars.netIncome}}, total assets {{money:vars.totalAssets}} and total equity {{money:vars.totalEquity}} at year end. Its peer Creekside Tea has no liabilities at all, so its ROE and ROA are both {{percent:vars.roePeer}}, the same as Mountain Haze’s ROE. Which reading is correct?

text.zh-TW: 山嵐的權益倍數是溪口的兩倍，資產有一半靠借來的錢，同樣的 ROE 背後風險比較高
text.en: Mountain Haze’s equity multiplier is twice Creekside’s; half its assets are funded by borrowing, so the same ROE carries more risk

feedback.zh-TW: 答對了。溪口沒有負債，權益倍數是一倍，ROE 等於 ROA。山嵐要靠兩倍的權益倍數，才把較低的 ROA 放大成同樣的 ROE。
feedback.en: Correct. Creekside has no liabilities, so its multiplier is one and ROE equals ROA. Mountain Haze needs a multiplier of two to lift its lower ROA to the same ROE.

text.zh-TW: 兩家的經營體質一樣好，因為股東拿到的報酬率相同，怎麼賺到的並不重要
text.en: The two businesses are equally sound, because shareholders earn the same return, and how it was earned does not matter

feedback.zh-TW: 股東的報酬率相同，來源卻不同：溪口靠資產本身的報酬，山嵐有一半靠槓桿。景氣轉差時，負債多的那一家 ROE 會掉得更快。
feedback.en: The shareholders’ return is the same, but its source differs: Creekside earns it from the assets themselves, while half of Mountain Haze’s comes from leverage. In a downturn, the more indebted firm’s ROE falls faster.

text.zh-TW: 山嵐比較安全，因為它用比較高的權益倍數，就做到和溪口一樣的 ROE
text.en: Mountain Haze is safer, because it matches Creekside’s ROE with a higher equity multiplier

feedback.zh-TW: 方向反了。權益倍數高代表負債多，利息與還款壓力都比較大；倍數高是風險的來源，不是安全的證明。
feedback.en: That is backwards. A higher equity multiplier means more liabilities and heavier interest and repayment pressure; a high multiplier is a source of risk, not proof of safety.

explanation.zh-TW: {{option:o_r3v0}}。ROE ＝ ROA × 權益倍數，所以溪口的權益倍數是一倍、山嵐是兩倍。同樣的 ROE 可以來自資產本身會賺（高 ROA），也可以來自借得多（高權益倍數）；判讀時一定要把 ROA 和權益倍數拆開看。
explanation.en: {{option:o_r3v0}}. ROE = ROA × equity multiplier, so Creekside’s multiplier is one and Mountain Haze’s is two. The same ROE can come from assets that earn well (high ROA) or from heavy borrowing (high multiplier); always split ROA and the multiplier apart when reading it.
